sourceInformation.perspective: Third person: island follow, mirror exercises, chase, high three-quarter and side views.
sourceInformation.tech: Pavilion 0.1.0 / Rust 1.98.1 / WASM / wgpu 30.0.1 / egui 0.36.2 / rapier 0.36.0 / cpal 0.18.2. Base: 49ef2ba.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Pastel cel-shaded rounded primitives, soft shadows and thin outlines; original resort props.
sourceInformation.animation: Pavilion puppets and 23 FIT clips: original exercise keys plus Mesh2Motion and 100STYLE adaptations.
sourceInformation.audio: Code-synthesised music, 32 effects and distinct gibberish voices. Seven original arrangements. Music defaults to 10%.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub ghost medley, client 1.4.0, for 1–4 players; local 2–4 guest hot-seat medley and personal ghosts.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless bots/scripts; controller, touch and audio stand-ins; Hub network harness; viewport/capture checks. No physical devices.
sourceInformation.research: Read PLAN/TASK, Pavilion engine guides/APIs and AI Hub README/client/harness from their public GitHub repositories.

testingFeedback: How many issues did testing catch? 16 distinct game/UI issues, all fixed; compiler errors and harness-only false positives are excluded. Details are in notes/feedback.md.
How many were critical or game breaking? 2 invalid asset-schema issues prevented startup. Both were corrected before packaging.
Most helpful test: the complete five-day bot playthrough on three seeds, paired with five-seed bot/idle/careless scoring checks for every activity.

Least helpful test: early browser checks with fixed short waits and exact JSON float equality; software rendering and f32 conversion caused false failures. State acknowledgements and tolerances replaced them.
engineFeedback: Most liked: one deterministic simulation, native puppet/primitive art and headless capture tools shared by browser and native builds.
Got stuck or guessed wrong: prop category/corner-radius validation and the custom input/menu seams needed local checks and reading engine source.
Most important custom system: the shared Balance Core and full resort state machine, with activity bots, saves, minutes and the finale.
Hardest part: connecting a controller-first game UI, browser inputs, audio sequencing and Hub status across several engine crates.

Engine changes: extended InputFrame and Game freezing, fit HUD/status and UI hit rectangles, figure tilt, bindings/browser bridge, sample-clock music/formant voices/audio buses, and splash/wake effects. Files are in pav_core, pav_ui, pav_app, pav_audio, pav_view and pav_tools.
One requested engine improvement: a first-class custom-game shell for menus, input mapping, saves, UI frames and browser/Hub hooks. This would remove most cross-crate integration work.
promptFeedback: Most liked: the concrete Balance Core, daily ritual and deadpan equipment cast gave the anthology a clear identity.
Confusing: the plan’s verified snippets described tested seams rather than an already integrated game; the actual build still required those engine changes.
Hardest: completing eleven distinct activities, five-day progression, procedural audio, controller UI and both multiplayer paths in one HTML.
What to change: provide the engine UI/input/browser seams as a reusable starter package, leaving more effort for activity feel, scene composition and writing.

aiHub.name: Wobble Wit
aiHub.tagline: A little less wobble. A little more you.
aiHub.description: Win a five-day holiday at a wellness resort staffed by talking gym equipment. Lean, breathe, step and splash through eleven activities, then try doing absolutely nothing.
aiHub.controls: Left stick/WASD/mouse lean; Cross/Space/click action; shoulders/Q/E steps; Triangle/Tab schedule; Options/Esc pause.
